<meta>continues from previous page: ...we will laugh to our hearts' content,</meta>

<term>EV.</term> What birds do I see here? <term>CA.</term> It is the patriarch of the college. Do not withdraw yourself; they have already finished drinking; sit down for a little while; when he has departed, we shall converse in our usual manner. <term>EV.</term> Come, I will adjure you to do what you were unwilling to do for me. Now that we are alone, tell me the whole story, for I would rather learn it from you. <term>CA.</term> Out of so many friends whom I thought loved me most of all, I now perceive that there was no one who gave me counsel more prudently or more like an elder than you, the youngest of all. <term>EV.</term> But in what manner did you overcome the affection of your parents? <term>CA.</term> First, it was through the wicked exhortations of the monks and nuns; then, my mother’s mind was shaken by my own prayers and coaxing; my father could not be persuaded by any means. At last, with all machines <note>that is, pressures or schemes</note> set in motion, he was conquered and overwhelmed rather than consenting. It was done over the wine cups; they threatened a horrible, wretched destruction if he refused his daughter to Christ. <term>EV.</term> O, the wickedness of the foolish! What happened next? <term>CA.</term> I was kept hidden at home for three days; meanwhile, some women from that college, whom they call <term>Conversas</term> <gloss>lay sisters or converts</gloss>, were always present, adding spirit to their exhortations so that I would persist in the holy proposal, and they were solicitously careful that no relative or companion should approach me who might seem likely to change my mind. In the meantime, the clothes and other things that pertained to the feast were being adorned. <term>EV.</term> How were you feeling in the meantime? Did you waver? <term>CA.</term> No, but I suffered something so horrific that I would rather die ten times over than endure it again. <term>EV.</term> I ask you, what is that? <term>CA.</term> I cannot speak of it. <term>EV.</term> What you have said to me, you have said to your friend. <term>CA.</term> Do you promise silence? <term>EV.</term> I was about to guarantee that, even if you had stipulated nothing. As if you did not know me yet.

<summary>Catharina recounts to Eubulus the intense social and emotional pressure she endured from monks, nuns, and her family to force her into religious life, describing a traumatic experience she has yet to fully disclose.</summary>
<keywords>Catharina, Eubulus, religious coercion, monastic life, parental authority, lay sisters</keywords>
